attempts.raw: {"patches": [{"section": "arc", "original": "That FY2023 step came from higher rates lifting net interest income 33.8%, with net interest income reaching 56.5% of revenue [D174][D162].", "type": "comparison", "text": "Net interest income rose 33.8% in FY2023 and reached 56.5% of revenue, up from 51.8% in FY2022 [D174][D162][D137]."}]}

sentences.text: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025, an 8.4% net interest income CAGR and 6.2% noninterest income CAGR [F1][F10][F11][F20][F111][F112][D5][D206].
The path was a step change rather than a smooth compound: revenue was $128.7 billion in FY2022 and $158 billion in FY2023, a 22.9% jump [D134][D159][D179].
Net interest income rose 33.8% in FY2023 and reached 56.5% of revenue, up from 51.8% in FY2022 [D174][D162][D137].
FY2025 growth slowed to 2.8%, with net interest income up 3.1% and noninterest income up 2.4% [D226][D221][D222].
North America remains the core, at 76.6% of revenue in FY2025, but contributed only 0.2pp of growth that year [D249][D251].
Asia-Pacific grew 17.3% and contributed 1.2pp, matching EMEA's 1.2pp on 9.5% growth [D300][D301][D275][D276].

Net interest income growth was driven by higher Markets net interest income, higher revolving balances in Card Services and higher wholesale deposit balances, largely offset by deposit margin compression [P28].
Noninterest revenue rose on higher Markets revenue, asset management fees and a $588 million First Republic-related gain, offset by the absence of the prior year's $7.9 billion Visa gain [P27].
Net income fell 2.6% while diluted EPS rose 1.4%, as the diluted share count fell 3.4% [D214][D216][D224].
The efficiency ratio was 52.4% in FY2025, below its 57.2% window median and near the 51.7% window low of FY2024 [D207][D333][D331].
Against seven bank peers, that efficiency ratio sits at the 0th percentile versus a 61.7% peer median [D336][D337].
Noninterest expense rose 4.2% to $95.6 billion, driven by higher compensation, brokerage and distribution fees, auto lease depreciation and technology and marketing investment [D225][X137][P26].
The credit-loss provision rose to 7.8% of revenue from 6.0%, above the 6.0% peer median [D208][D185][D341].
The higher provision reflected net portfolio increases, credit-quality changes on client-specific exposures, updated leveraged-loan loss assumptions and estimated borrower-fraud losses [P15].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank; it was -$148 billion in FY2025 against $57.0 billion of net income [F60][F30].
The outflow came from higher trading assets, higher securities borrowed, net loan originations held-for-sale and higher other assets [P21].
Capital return is the better test: buybacks plus dividends of $48.2 billion were 85% of FY2025 net income [D205][F30].
Return on average equity was 16.1% in FY2025, at the 100th percentile against a 11.8% peer median [D213][D338][D339].
Loans rose to 57.3% of deposits from 55.0%, and the allowance held at 1.8% of loans [D211][D188][D212].
Loans grew $121.1 billion, driven by higher CIB Markets loans and securities-based lending in AWM on higher client demand [P4].
Buybacks of $31.6 billion and dividends of $16.6 billion were funded alongside a $269.5 billion financing inflow, and the diluted share count fell 3.4% [X102][X112][F80][D224].
Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy's pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, differing by up to 0.10% [R1][F26][X16][F30][X20].
The gap is immaterial to growth rates but the 10-K figures should be used where precision matters [R1].
Criticized wholesale exposure rose to $48.5 billion, or 3.4% of wholesale credit exposure, from $44.7 billion, driven by downgrades and new commitments [P2].
The provision at 7.8% of revenue sits in the 75th percentile of four bank peers, so credit cost is above the peer median [D208][D340][D341].
Watch the efficiency ratio: a move above the 57.2% window median would reverse the FY2024-FY2025 cost discipline, reported in the next 10-K [D333][D207].
Watch the credit-loss provision against its 7.8% of revenue level; a further rise above the 6.0% peer median would confirm the deteriorating credit trend [D208][D341].
Watch net interest income growth against the 3.1% FY2025 rate, with deposit margin compression the stated offset [D221][P28].
